title: Iterated Ex gives a Kan replacement preserving finite limits
statement:
Use simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. Let $\operatorname{Sd}(\Delta^n)$ be the ordinary nerve of the poset of nonempty subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n\}$ ordered by inclusion. Define $(\operatorname{Ex}K)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{Sd}(\Delta^n),K)$ with operators induced by image of subsets under monotone maps. The map sending a subset to its largest element gives a natural last-vertex map $\operatorname{Sd}(\Delta^n)\to\Delta^n$, and hence $j_K:K\to\operatorname{Ex}K$. Define
$$\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}K=\operatorname{colim}\bigl(K\xrightarrow{j_K}\operatorname{Ex}K\xrightarrow{j_{\operatorname{Ex}K}}\operatorname{Ex}^2K\longrightarrow\cdots\bigr).$$
Then $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}K$ is Kan for every $K$, the natural map $K\to\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}K$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, and the functor $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}$ preserves finite limits. Preservation of finite products means that the canonical maps to the products of the images, including the terminal-object comparison, are isomorphisms; these canonical comparisons and the natural unit commute with product projections.

source.place: Kerodon Section 3.3.6, Construction 3.3.6.1 and Propositions 3.3.6.4, 3.3.6.7 and 3.3.6.9, section Tag 00ZA (Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag). No Stacks tag supplies this simplicial Kan replacement.

proof.text: Postcomposition defines $\operatorname{Ex}(u)$ for every simplicial map $u$. Since a monotone map commutes with taking the maximum of a nonempty subset, the last-vertex maps commute with all simplex operators; hence $j$ is a natural transformation. Each $j_X$ is degreewise injective: the map $[n]\to\mathcal P_+([n])$, $a\mapsto\{0,\ldots,a\}$, is monotone and its nerve is a section of $\lambda_n$. Thus precomposition with $\lambda_n$ is injective on maps into $X$. In particular all stages $X_m=\operatorname{Ex}^mK$ embed in the degreewise colimit. Degreewise colimits have the simplicial universal property because each operator is induced on representatives and the functorial identities hold on representatives [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. For a map $u:K\to L$, the maps $\operatorname{Ex}^m(u)$ commute with the transitions by naturality of $j$ and thus induce $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}(u)$ on colimits. Identities and composition hold on every stage, and the stage-zero maps therefore form a natural unit.

source.place: Construction 3.3.6.1 and Proposition 3.3.6.2; online source read 2026-10-17, archive WANTED; agent supplies the expanded argument.

proof.text:
Use [lem-coef-subdivision-face-poset-calculus] for the subdivision adjunction and the face-poset description. Fix $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$, and put $V=[n]$, $P=\mathcal P_+(V)$, and $Q=P\setminus\{V,V\setminus\{i\}\}$. The faces of $\Lambda_i^n$ are exactly the nonempty subsets omitting some vertex other than $i$. For a chain in $Q$, its largest member contains all the maxima and omits a vertex other than $i$, so the image-of-maxima set is again in $Q$. The cited identifications give
$$\operatorname{Sd}\Lambda_i^n=N(Q),\quad \operatorname{Sd}^2\Lambda_i^n=N(\operatorname{Ch}(Q)),\quad \operatorname{Sd}^2\Delta^n=N(\operatorname{Ch}(P)).$$
On these descriptions $\operatorname{Sd}(\lambda_{\Lambda_i^n})$ is the nerve of the map sending a chain $\{S_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq S_r\}$ in $Q$ to $\{\max S_0,\ldots,\max S_r\}\in Q$: this is the image-of-faces rule applied to the vertex map $S\mapsto\max S$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.6.9 (00ZK), reduction to face posets, using Proposition 3.3.3.17 (00YL); online source read 2026-10-17, archive WANTED; agent supplies the expanded argument.

proof.text:
Define a function on vertices of $P$ by $b(S)=i$ for $S=V$ or $S=V\setminus\{i\}$ and $b(S)=\max S$ otherwise. For a nonempty chain $C\subseteq P$, put $r(C)=\{b(S):S\in C\}$. This set is nonempty and belongs to $Q$. Indeed, if $C$ has an allowed member, choose its largest allowed member $T$; all allowed members are subsets of $T$, so $r(C)\subseteq T\cup\{i\}$. Since $T\in Q$, it omits a vertex different from $i$, and so does $r(C)$. If $C$ has no allowed member, $r(C)=\{i\}$, which also omits another vertex because $n\geq1$. For $C\subseteq C'$, $r(C)\subseteq r(C')$, so $r:\operatorname{Ch}(P)\to Q$ is monotone. If $C\subseteq Q$, every $b(S)$ is $\max S$, so its restriction is exactly the map of step 2. Taking nerves therefore constructs
$$R:\operatorname{Sd}^2\Delta^n\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sd}\Lambda_i^n,\qquad R|_{\operatorname{Sd}^2\Lambda_i^n}=\operatorname{Sd}(\lambda_{\Lambda_i^n}).$$
The nerve of a monotone map is obtained by applying it to each entry of a weakly increasing sequence; this commutes with restriction, so no extension theorem is hidden here [lem-coef-subdivision-face-poset-calculus].

source.place: Proposition 3.3.6.9 (00ZK), explicit finite-poset extension; landing in Q and monotonicity expanded; online source read 2026-10-17, archive WANTED; agent supplies the expanded argument.

proof.text: Let $f:\Lambda_i^n\to\operatorname{Ex}X$ and let $\bar f:\operatorname{Sd}\Lambda_i^n\to X$ be its adjoint under [lem-coef-subdivision-face-poset-calculus]. The map $\bar fR:\operatorname{Sd}^2\Delta^n\to X$ transposes twice to $h:\Delta^n\to\operatorname{Ex}^2X$. Its restriction is the double transpose of $\bar f\operatorname{Sd}(\lambda_{\Lambda_i^n})$, by step 3. This is precisely $j_{\operatorname{Ex}X}f$: first $j_{\operatorname{Ex}X}f$ transposes to $f\lambda_{\Lambda_i^n}$ since $j$ transposes to $\lambda$; transposing that map once more gives $\bar f\operatorname{Sd}(\lambda_{\Lambda_i^n})$ by naturality of the adjunction. Thus every horn in $\operatorname{Ex}X$ fills after applying the transition to $\operatorname{Ex}^2X$. In particular the restriction involves $\operatorname{Sd}(\lambda_A)$, not $\lambda_{\operatorname{Sd}A}$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.6.9 (00ZK), double-adjunction identification of the required restriction; online source read 2026-10-17, archive WANTED; agent supplies the expanded argument.

proof.text: Now take $f:\Lambda_i^n\to\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}K$. This horn is generated by the finitely many faces of $\Delta^n$ other than face $i$. Choose representatives at a common stage for their images, then increase the stage to some $m\geq1$. The face compatibility equations hold there because the stage maps into the colimit are injective by step 1; hence these face maps glue to $f_m:\Lambda_i^n\to X_m$. Explicitly, on any simplex of the horn choose a containing face and apply its simplicial operator to that face's representative; on intersections the two expressions agree by those equations. Apply step 4 with $X=X_{m-1}$ and then map $X_{m+1}$ to the colimit to obtain a filler of $f$. For $n=1$ the horn has one vertex and the same argument has no intersection equations. The characterization of Kan complexes by fillers for these horns, with $n\geq1$ and both outer horns included, is [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. Therefore $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}K$ is Kan, including when $K$ is empty.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.6.9 (00ZK), passage from a finite horn to one finite stage; online source read 2026-10-17, archive WANTED; agent supplies the expanded argument.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-ex-comparison-weak-equivalence], every transition $X_m\to X_{m+1}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. The finite composite $u_m:K\to X_m$ is consequently a weak equivalence, using composition in the model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]; $u_0$ is the identity. These maps form a natural transformation from the constant $\mathbf N$-diagram $K$ to $(X_m)$. Apply [lem-coef-filtered-colimit-weak-equivalences] with the small filtered category $\mathbf N$ to this transformation. The colimit of the constant diagram is $K$ (a cocone is a single map because $0\to m$ for every $m$), and the induced map is exactly the stage-zero inclusion $K\to\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}K$. It is therefore a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.6.7, using Theorem 3.3.5.1 (00Z2) and Proposition 3.2.8.3 (00XE); online source read 2026-10-17, archive WANTED; agent supplies the expanded argument.

proof.text:
Let $D:J\to\mathrm{sSet}$ be a finite diagram and put $L=\lim_JD$, formed degreewise as compatible tuples. A map from any simplicial set $T$ into $L$ is exactly a family of maps $T\to D(a)$ commuting with every arrow of $J$: the inverse sends the family to its tuple in each degree. Hence for $T=\operatorname{Sd}\Delta^n$,
$$(\operatorname{Ex}L)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(T,L)\cong\lim_{a\in J}\operatorname{Hom}(T,D(a))=(\lim_{a\in J}\operatorname{Ex}D(a))_n.$$
These bijections commute with all operators, since both sides act by precomposition with the same maps of subdivided simplices. This proves preservation of finite limits by $\operatorname{Ex}$. Inducting on $m$, composition of these canonical bijections proves it for every $\operatorname{Ex}^m$; the case $m=0$ is the identity. Empty $J$ gives the singleton set in each degree [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set].

source.place: Proposition 3.3.6.4, preservation of limits by Ex expanded directly from its Hom formula; online source read 2026-10-17, archive WANTED; agent supplies the expanded argument.

proof.text:
The comparisons of step 7 commute with the transitions in $m$, since after each projection both composites are the same by naturality of $j$. For each degree $n$ apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] to the diagram of sets $(m,a)\mapsto(\operatorname{Ex}^mD(a))_n$. Its first index is the small filtered category $\mathbf N$, and its second index is the given finite category $J$. We obtain the canonical bijection
$$(\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}L)_n\cong\varinjlim_m\lim_{a\in J}(\operatorname{Ex}^mD(a))_n\cong\lim_{a\in J}\varinjlim_m(\operatorname{Ex}^mD(a))_n.$$
All maps here are induced by projections and coprojections, so applying a simplicial operator before or after gives the same representatives. The bijections thus assemble to an isomorphism $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}(\lim_JD)\to\lim_J\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}D$. This proves preservation of finite limits, including the empty limit.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.6.4; Stacks Tag 002W (categories.tex, lemma-directed-commutes) for the interchange; online source read 2026-10-17, archive WANTED; agent supplies the expanded argument.

proof.text: For a finite family $(K_a)$ the comparison just proved is the unique map $c:\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}(\prod_aK_a)\to\prod_a\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}K_a$ whose $a$th component is $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}(p_a)$. Thus $p_a c=\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}(p_a)$. If $u_K:K\to\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}K$ denotes the stage-zero map, its naturality gives $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}(p_a)u_{\prod K_a}=u_{K_a}p_a$. After composing with every projection this is the equality $c\,u_{\prod K_a}=\prod_a u_{K_a}$. For the empty family, both the comparison and these equalities are the unique maps to the terminal simplicial set. This supplies the stated compatibility of canonical comparisons and unit with product projections.
